name: PagerDuty MCP
tagline: Manage incidents, alerts, and on-call schedules from your AI agent.
shortDescription: The official PagerDuty MCP server. List active incidents, acknowledge alerts, trigger new incidents, list on-call schedules, and look up services. The canonical way to give an agent incident response access.
longDescription:
## What it is

The PagerDuty MCP server, maintained by PagerDuty. Exposes the PagerDuty API as MCP tools: list active incidents, get incident details, acknowledge/resolve/escalate alerts, trigger new incidents, list on-call schedules, and look up service owners.

## Why we recommend it

If your on-call rotation is on PagerDuty, this is the cleanest way to let your agent help with incident response. It can pull current incidents, identify who's on-call, check the runbook attached to a service, and summarize what's happening — all in chat. The auth is your standard PagerDuty REST API key.

## When to use it

- Incident response: agent pulls current incidents, identifies responders
- Postmortem assistance: agent fetches the timeline of a resolved incident
- On-call awareness: agent checks who's on-call before paging someone manually
- Alert inspection: agent acknowledges low-priority alerts and explains them
installInstructions:
1. Create a PagerDuty REST API key at https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/api-access-keys
2. Set: `PAGERDUTY_API_KEY`
3. `uvx pagerduty-mcp`

**Security note:** Use a key scoped to read-only or limited-write. Never give the agent full admin access to PagerDuty.
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. PagerDuty pricing varies by plan; free for up to 5 users.
